key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a scalable route to improve photocatalytic carbon conversion by combining catalyst design for CO2 activation with a renewable, carbon-negative co-feed.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs/Ba to increase surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption and Bi lone pairs to promote polarization and charge separation.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae as sacrificial agents.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on maintaining microalgae stability and integrating biomass handling with photocatalytic reactor operation.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
